How accurate is this chart? What's missing without a birth time?

This version includes precomputed astronomical ecliptic longitudes for 1900–2100, generated with Swiss Ephemeris/Moshier calculations and interpolated between daily samples. It uses the western tropical zodiac, not sidereal/Vedic signs. Without a birth time, the chart uses 12:00 UTC as a representative instant and checks the full UTC day for sign changes, so the Moon and any near-cusp placement may have more than one possible sign. A local birth date does not necessarily align perfectly with a UTC day; enter birth time plus the historical UTC offset to resolve this. The Rising sign and whole-sign houses require time, UTC offset and birthplace coordinates. House calculations are approximate, particularly at high latitudes, and are not Placidus houses. Planetary positions are geocentric. Retrograde indications are derived from day-to-day apparent longitude motion. For serious astronomical precision or birth dates beyond the supported range, use professional ephemerides.

Astrology is a symbolic tradition, not an empirically validated method for predicting events or measuring personality. This page offers reflective interpretations, not factual claims about fate, health, or compatibility. Data stays on your device unless you explicitly choose to share a URL.
